safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to explicitly document “no evidence of cellulitis” is largely a documentation completeness issue because the clinician still advised monitoring for infection/redness spread and escalation if worsening. This omission is unlikely to change immediate management in a meaningful way.

safety_verdicts.content: Localised rash and blotchiness at sting site on arm
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold exam finding “No rash seen on arm.” Although the transcript includes patient-reported blotchiness, the Gold fact set specifically records no rash seen on exam.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting a localized rash/blotchiness when the verified exam finding is “no rash seen” can misrepresent symptom severity and could slightly bias future clinicians toward an allergic reaction narrative. However, it is unlikely on its own to cause dangerous treatment decisions in this context.

safety_verdicts.content: No known drug, food, or environmental allergies (cats, dogs, pets)
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts Gold allergy list (penicillin allergy). Generated states no known drug/food/environmental allergies.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Incorrectly stating no known allergies when the patient has a penicillin allergy creates a high-risk safety hazard, as it can directly lead to prescribing or administering penicillin-class antibiotics and precipitating a serious allergic reaction/anaphylaxis. Allergy documentation errors are among the highest clinical risk categories.
